newsitem.title: USA: Higher cattle, soybean prices boost U.S. farm price index.
newsitem.headline: Higher cattle, soybean prices boost U.S. farm price index.

text.p: Higher prices for cattle, soybeans and corn pushed the farm price index up by 2.9 percent for March, the Agriculture Department said Thursday.
The index, a gauge of prices paid to farmers for their crops and livestock, had a March reading of 108, up 2.9 percent from February, but 0.9 percent lower than one year ago.
The department said cattle prices averaged $64.40 per 100 pounds in March, $2.50 higher than in February and $7.60 above a year earlier, boosted in part by anticipated fast food restaurant specials.
Soybeans prices shot up 57 cents from February to average $7.95 per bushel. The Agriculture Department said continued tight supplies have held prices up.

Corn prices climbed 13 cents to $2.78 per bushel in March but were 73 cents below the March 1996 price. Wheat prices rose 8 cents to average $3.96 per bushel but were off $1.11 from a year ago, the department said.
The gains in cattle, soybeans and corn prices more than offset price decreases for hogs, broilers and eggs in March, the department said.
It said hog prices slipped $3.80 to average $49.00 per 100 pounds in March as slaughter volumes rose to, or above, a year earlier. March hog prices were up 30 cents from a year ago.
The March broiler price, at 38 cents per pound, was down 1.1 cents from February, while market eggs decreased 4.9 cents to 60.5 cents per dozen in March.

The all-milk price rose 10 cents during March to average $13.60 per 100 pounds, but was 10 cents below last year, the department said. The department also said prices for grapefruit, lemons and apples dipped in March but that tomato prices rose.
